newsitem.title: USA: Tractebel trading power in the U.S.
newsitem.headline: Tractebel trading power in the U.S.

text.p: Tractebel SA made its first trade in the U.S. power market last month, becoming the first European utility in the market, chief executive Baron Philippe Bodson told a news conference.

The company's new trading subsidiary, Tractebel Energy Marketing Inc, officially began operation April 1, a full week after its first electricity trade, according to the new unit's trading chief, William L. Coorsh.
Tractabel is "the first continental utility to be involved in U.S. energy marketing," Baron Bodson said.
As a result, the company expects to "be very well positioned" when power trading starts in Europe, he said.
He does not expect natural gas trading in Europe, stating "the dream of competition in Europe is the dream of the European commission" because of the limited number of suppliers.
Trading volume for the recently initiated natural gas futures contract on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) has been thin.
With four natural gas suppliers, Baron Badson explained, "one can corner the market."

Tractabel chose to start a trading firm from scratch instead of acquiring an existing firm "because it is a lot cheaper," explained Wim Heyselberghs, senior vice president of distribution operations for Tractebel Electricity and Gas International.
He said the new firm will market and trade electricity, natural gas and fuel oil at both the wholesale and retail levels "mainly in the U.S. Northeast and eastern Canada."
That's where another Tractabell subsidiary, CRSS Inc, has most of its non-utility power plants, he noted.
By year end, Heyselberghs said, Tractebel Energy Marketing will have 20 employees in offices in Houston, Boston and Montreal.
The new units' objective is "not maximum volume," he said, but to be the "most profitable" trader.
Tractebel officials declined to discuss the company's profit and volume goals.
